# n8n: MCP access token (instance-level MCP, API key tab)

`n8n-2` · Personal access token · person. n8n generates a personal access token per user for the instance MCP server, sent as Authorization: Bearer to the /mcp-server/http endpoint.

Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant. "No docs found" means vendor documentation does not say either way.

| Question | Answer | Why | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identify: Admin can list all of them | Partial | API-key MCP clients do not appear in the Connected clients list; their tool calls show only in the n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called log with authType api_key (Enterprise log streaming). | Where: No list. Settings > Log Streaming: subscribe to n8n.audit.mcp; filter n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called on authType=api_key, group by userId (Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > View all lists only OAuth clients) |
| Protect: Admin can block or require approval | Yes | Enable/Disable MCP access; N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp | Enable/Disable MCP access: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connection details · N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp: Environment variable |
| Protect: SSO and MFA rules apply | No docs found | No vendor documentation found. |  |
| Protect: IP restriction | No docs found | Not documented. |  |
| Protect: Expires automatically | No docs found | No expiry documented; rotate manually |  |
| Detect: Usage appears in logs | Yes | authType, userId | Where: Settings > Log Streaming > Add new destination > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter authType=api_key and userId |
| Detect: Data reads appear in logs | Yes | n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called | Where: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: n8n.audit.mcp; filter event n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called with authType=api_key; see toolName, workflowId |
| Respond: Revocation ends active access | Yes | Rotation revokes the previous token; no token creation event documented. | Where: Token owner: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect > API key tab > generate new token (revokes old). Admin: Connection details > MCP status > Disable (revokes all clients) · Command: N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp (self-hosted, removes MCP endpoints) |
| Respond: Stops working when user is removed | No docs found | No vendor documentation found. |  |

## Protect: what an admin can configure

### Admin controls
- **Enable/Disable MCP access** (Disable; all plans; default off). Turns the instance MCP server on or off; disabling disconnects every client. Where: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connection details.
- **N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp** (Disable; Self-hosted only; default off). Removes MCP endpoints entirely. Where: Environment variable.
- **Per-workflow MCP access** (Limit resources; all plans; default off). Only workflows marked Available in MCP can be read in full, run or edited. Where: Workflow settings > Available in MCP; Settings > Instance-level MCP > Workflows enabled.

- Network: unknown (checked at unknown). Not documented.
- Lifetime: No expiry documented; rotate manually. Renewal: Generating a new token revokes the previous one.
- Keyless option: not_applicable. Static bearer token.
- Conditions: API-key clients do not appear in the Connected clients list, so admins cannot revoke them there.

## Detect: what gets logged
- Token prefix: not established

### Logs
- Log streaming: n8n.audit.mcp.*: Enterprise; from n8n 2.34.0.

### Fields that identify the credential
- `authType` (n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called): api_key for any non-OAuth bearer token.
- `userId` (n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called): Token owner.

### Lifecycle events
- use: `n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called` Includes toolName, workflowId, status.
- other: `n8n.audit.mcp.access.updated` Instance MCP turned on/off.

### Correlate on
`userId`, `toolName`, `workflowId`

### API calls a holder can make, and whether they are logged
- discovery (bulk): `MCP tool search_workflows`. Previews of all workflows the user can view Logged: yes (`n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called`). Enterprise log streaming
- collection: `MCP tool execute_workflow`. Runs MCP-enabled workflows Logged: yes (`n8n.audit.mcp.tool.called`). 

### What to look for (analyst guidance)
- authType=api_key tool calls from a user who normally uses OAuth
- execute_workflow or search_workflows bursts

## Respond: how to revoke it
- Admin: **Rotate MCP access token**. Generating a new token revokes the old one. Where: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect > API key tab.

Owner rotates the token (revokes old). Admin can disable instance MCP, which revokes all clients. Live access ends on revocation: yes. Rotation revokes the previous token; no token creation event documented.
